page: Microsoft Azure D248s_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 series, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel processors and provides 248 vCPUs coupled with 992.0 GB of system memory. This configuration adheres to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, yielding exactly 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The virtual machine does not include onboard local storage disks or integrated graphics processing units. Instead, it relies entirely on remote storage volumes and is designated as Premium Storage capable for external persistent disk attachments. Networking configurations omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, necessitating network address translation or provisioned public IPs for external routing.

Because of its high core count and large physical memory pool, the D248s_v7 offers substantial resource density for multi-threaded enterprise workloads. The absence of local disk drives avoids hardware storage coupling, shifting operational storage throughput and latency requirements entirely to attached network block storage.

This server type is architecturally configured for large-scale enterprise applications that require massive parallel CPU concurrency and memory capacity without needing dedicated GPU hardware. Typical deployment targets include relational database systems, extensive data processing pipelines, enterprise resource planning services, and distributed microservice clusters.
description: Microsoft Azure D248s_v7 is a high-density, general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 248 dedicated vCPUs and 992.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a uniform 1:4 resource ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPUs and contains no local disk storage, depending on external Premium Storage volumes for all persistent storage operations. It also does not include complimentary public IPv4 networking. Designed for extensive concurrent processing, the D248s_v7 consolidates significant compute and memory capacity on a single node, making it suitable for large enterprise databases, intensive backend services, and distributed compute workloads that do not require local ephemeral storage or hardware acceleration.
